stories.title: US bars IT firm from sponsoring green cards, imposes $2m settlement
summary: WASHINGTON: The United States has barred California-based technology company Cloudera Inc. from participating in the employment-based green card process for two years and secured a $2 million settlement over allegations that it discriminated against qualified American workers.

It resolves a lawsuit filed by the Justice Department in April, alleging that Cloudera violated the Immigration and Nationality Act by discriminating against American workers while recruiting for seven positions under the Permanent Labour Certification, or PERM, programme.
During the debarment period, the company cannot participate in the PERM programme to sponsor foreign workers for employment-based green cards.

stories.title: Rubio heads to India for 'trade diplomacy'
summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio heads to India on Tuesday for his second official visit to the country this year, as he pursues an Asian tour blending diplomacy and trade.

After a trip to Uzbekistan, where he called for stronger partnerships with Central Asian countries, Rubio will head to Mumbai to hold talks with Foreign Minister Subrahmanyam Jaishankar and meet business leaders.
Rubio’s visit comes as the two countries struggle to finalise a trade deal that has been a source of repeated tensions.

The research, titled ‘Detection of Rabies Virus RNA in Dog-Bite Wounds in a Rabies-Endemic Area: Evidence from an Observational Cohort Study,’ revealed a strikingly high level of rabies virus circulation in the local canine population, with the virus detected in 64pc of samples.

summary: ISLAMABAD: The Senate on Monday passed a bill that sought to allow former lawmakers to have blue passports even if they had not served a full term in the National Assembly (NA) or Senate.

Official blue passports are issued to key constitutional, government and judicial office holders, senior bureaucrats and their eligible dependents, allowing them visa-free entry to 55 countries, including 22 European countries.

Speaking on blue passports in the Senate, Chaudhry said the number of these official passports issued in the country had been reduced from 75,000 to 45,000 after European countries and Canada raised reservations.

stories.title: Two sentenced in FC personnel’s murder case in Gilgit-Baltistan
summary: GILGIT: An anti-terrorism court (ATC) in Gilgit-Baltistan on Monday sentenced the prime accused to death and his accomplice to life imprisonment in the murder case of a Frontier Corps (FC) personnel at a forest checkpost in Thore, Diamer.
ATC Judge Rehmat Shah heard the case involving the murder of FC personnel Muhammad Gul Sher at the Thore checkpost in Diamer.
After finding the accused guilty, the court sentenced the prime accused, Usman Shafi, to death and his accomplice, Gulzar, to life imprisonment.

stories.title: 20 abducted police recruits ‘recovered safely’ in Kalat
summary: QUETTA: The 20 police recruits from the Kalat Police Training Centre, who were abducted by unidentified men on Friday, have been safely recovered, officials told Dawn.
The recruits, who were kidnapped while en route to Noshki from Kalat in a private van, were recovered from the Mangochar area of Kalat district, sources said.
A senior police officer told Dawn that “all personnel are safe and sound”.

stories.title: Burnt bridges
summary: A WEEK after the federal government imposed governor’s rule and emergency in KP, PPP Chairperson Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari invited the opposition to engage ‘positively’ with the centre, saying this could lead to their reversal.
The latter party would do well to recall that, in 2009, when its government in Punjab was dismissed and governor’s rule imposed, it had itself joined a ‘long march’ on Islamabad to press its demands.
It will not be easy to build bridges with the opposition, but the PML-N, more than any other party, has the power to concede some ground to show goodwill.

stories.title: JUI-F urges rivals to stop ‘anti-Fazl campaign’
summary: ISLAMABAD: JUI-F Punjab General Secretary Hafiz Naseer Ahmed Ahrar on Monday urged the party’s political opponents to refrain from what he described as a campaign of character assassination against JUI-F chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman.
The JUI-F leader said his party’s struggle to transform Pakistan into an Islamic welfare state would continue under Maulana Fazlur Rehman’s leadership.

He said that after gaining public support in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Balochistan and Sindh, the party was also witnessing growing confidence among the people of Punjab. “Insha Allah, JUI-F will emerge as a force for the people’s deliverance in Punjab and across Pakistan,” he said.

stories.title: Dispute over Zangali checkpost disrupts Torkham operations
summary: KHYBER: The repatriation of Afghan families was suspended for about two hours, while staff members of government offices were asked to leave after a dispute over the repair or construction of a controversial checkpost on the Afghan side of the Torkham border emerged on Monday.
Sabir Khan, a resident of Torkham, told Dawn that the repatriation of Afghans resumed after about two hours and the Customs and immigration offices reopened.

Customs and immigration officials later confirmed that their operations, including the clearance of belongings of returning Afghan families and immigration procedures, had resumed after the Afghan authorities suspended construction work on the disputed checkpost.

stories.title: Four capital police officials arrested for ‘dacoity’ at Chinese nationals’ house
summary: ISLAMABAD: Four capital police officials allegedly involved in a dacoity at the house of Chinese nationals in the capital’s F-7/1 sector have been arrested, a police officer confirmed.
In the latest incident, a gang of dacoits in police uniforms raided a house in F-7/1 and looted Rs2 million in cash and a mobile phone worth Rs15,000.
Their involvement was exposed during the investigation into a dacoity on Sept 13, when gunmen dressed in police uniforms raided the house of two Chinese nationals in G-10/4 and looted Rs8 million.

stories.title: Number of checkposts in capital reduced from 24 to 12: IG

stories.title: Providing relief to fraud victims: Police for making offences under Section 420 non-bailable
summary: Also issue new SOPs for FIRs under Section 406 of the PPC dealing with breach of trust as per SC judgements He says that most complaints of fraud and cheating were liable to be treated as a criminal offence under Section 420.

stories.title: PM warns against resistance to FBR reforms
summary: ISLAMABAD: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Monday warned tax officers that resistance to the ongoing reforms in the Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) would not be tolerated, directing the authorities to implement proposed measures to minimise the country’s tax gap.
The prime minister’s warning came during a weekly briefing on tax reforms, following a call for a pen-down strike by the Inland Revenue Officers Association.

According to an official announcement by the Prime Minister’s Secretariat, PM Shehbaz directed that the pace of FBR reforms be accelerated, noting that the initial results of the ongoing measures were encouraging.

stories.title: Punjab backs consecutive sentences in heinous crimes
summary: Where multiple lives were unlawfully taken, each offence required independent penal recognition, it said, adding that merging all sentences into a single concurrent term would dilute the gravity of additional offences and equate the taking of one life with that of several.

The legislature had acknowledged this limitation and, through the Criminal Laws (Amendment) Act, 2021, introduced imprisonment for the remainder of a convict’s natural life as a punishment under Sections 375-A (gang rape) and 376 (punishment for rape) of PPC, the opinion noted.
It argued that the substantial reduction in the period actually served made it particularly important for courts to avoid a mechanical or casual approach when ordering sentences to run concurrently.

stories.title: Balochistan MPAs seek recovery of ‘abducted’ Hindu girl
summary: QUETTA: Treasury and opposition members in the Balochistan Assembly on Monday demanded the immediate recovery of a 14-year-old Hindu girl, and action against the man accused of abducting her from Sibi.

Dr Ashok Kumar, a PML-N minority member, raised the issue, saying the girl had reportedly been taken from Sibi a few days ago and shifted to Sindh, where she was allegedly forcibly converted and married.
He urged the provincial government to contact its Sindh counterpart immediately and ensure the girl’s safe recovery.

stories.title: CDF Munir to visit Tehran today
summary: ISLAMABAD: Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir is due to visit Tehran on Tuesday (today), according to a Pakistani official and Iranian media.
The scheduled visit follows earlier talks between Field Marshal Munir and Iranian leaders in the summer that focused on measures to prevent further escalation and reopening of the Strait of Hormuz.
